dct_title_s: Nepal Flood 2026 Flood Affected Area, Bhote Koshi and Trishuli
dct_description_sm: OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps vector layers for the area flooded in the 2026 Bhote Koshi and Trishuli flood in Nepal, and the ground immediately around it. The area of interest is the observed flood extent of 27 August 2026 widened by 200 metres. The extent itself was mapped from drone, Landsat, PlanetScope and Sentinel imagery and is published here as its own resource, so the water line can be separated from the margin around it. That margin brings in buildings and roads beside the water, so a feature being in this dataset is not evidence that it was flooded or damaged. Clip to the Flood Extent resource when you need figures for the water itself. The area follows the river from Rasuwagadhi to the Narayani confluence, across Bagmati and Gandaki Provinces and the districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitawan. Every layer holds what is standing and what has been lost, so buildings and roads do not vanish from a download once mappers record them as destroyed. `status` says Standing, Damaged or Destroyed, and the Destroyed and Damaged Features layer gathers everything marked destroyed or damaged in one place. Most layers come in two versions. The OpenStreetMap ones are rebuilt straight from OpenStreetMap through the day, so they carry volunteer work as it lands. The Overture ones fuse Microsoft, Google and OpenStreetMap, which reaches ground volunteers have not mapped yet, but they follow Overture's own release cycle and will not show mapping done during this response. Overture is wider, OpenStreetMap is current: for damage work prefer OpenStreetMap and use Overture where its coverage is thin. Mapping task boundaries from the Tasking Manager campaign show where volunteers are being asked to map. The bridge damage assessment is reported from the ground by volunteers and lists road bridges with their condition after the flood, deck length where measured, and administrative codes from the same boundaries as the other layers. For the wider 1 km river corridor under assessment, use [Nepal Flood 2026 River Corridor](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl_corridor). AI-scored building damage from post-event imagery is published separately as [Nepal Flood 2026: fAIr Damage Assessment](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl_buildings_damage). Subscribe to the dataset for updates as mapping progresses. - Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/), NAXA and volunteer field reports - Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)
dct_publisher_sm: OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps, volunteer field reports
